content.text:
The drawing shows a sulfur atom with these substituents:
- one S=O double bond,
- one S=N double bond, where the nitrogen carries SO2CF3,
- a CF3 group (highlighted with the orange circle),
- a phenyl ring.

This is a sulfoximine-type compound, a trifluoromethyl phenyl sulfonimidoyl species, N-triflyl S-trifluoromethyl S-phenyl sulfoximine. The sulfur is S(VI), bonded to O (double), N (double), CF3 and Ph.

The N substituent is SO2CF3, so the nitrogen is attached to a sulfonyl sulfur that carries two oxygens and a CF3.

The sulfur is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the drawing uses plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: O=S(=NS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)(C(F)(F)F)c1ccccc1
